title: History 15: The size era: FP8, GGUF and 4-bit formats arrive
hook: Each format answers one question: what do the weights share? The same test across all of them shows why int4 with one scale is ruined, and why fp8 hardly notices an outlier.

unchecked: We read the abstracts of the papers, not their full text.
The weights are synthetic. We measured no real model and rendered no pictures.
The two block rows are a simple stand-in, not the exact algorithm of any named format.
We did not compare GGUF with native formats for speed. The line from main.py is the project's own claim.
We don't name a GGUF pack here and did not test one.
We did not trace which real 4-bit format moved to block scales when. The lab shows the effect, not the history.
